title: Isotropic Nanoscale Quantum Sensor at Room-Temperature
authors: Daniel T. Möller, Baha Sakar, Ekrem T. Güldeste, Dhruv Wadhwani, Olt Gashi, Daniel A. García Vaca, Mokessh K. Ciwan, Simone P. Crozier, Christian Laube, Sirswa K. Shree Ram, Matteo Slaviero, Nabeel Aslam
abstract: Color-center based quantum sensors provide nanoscale resolution under ambient conditions, yet their applicability remains limited. Because the quantization axes are locked to the host lattice, conventional color centers suffer severe signal loss in off-axis magnetic fields. To address this, we report an isotropic magnetometer enabled by the neutrally charged nitrogen-vacancy center (NV0) in diamond. Here, spin-to-charge dynamics yield an NV0-dark spin pair whose quantization axis dynamically aligns with the external field. Read out through NV charge-state-selective fluorescence, this system exhibits microsecond room-temperature coherence and nanotesla sensitivity for arbitrary field directions. We demonstrate alignment-free mapping of steep field gradients and single paramagnetic micro-targets, alongside isotropic readout from randomly oriented nanodiamonds. Resolving longstanding orientation constraints, this platform unlocks unrestricted nanoscale magnetometry across life sciences and quantum materials.
summary: This paper introduces an isotropic nanoscale quantum sensor based on the $	ext{NV}^0$ center in diamond, overcoming the major limitation of conventional sensors whose sensitivity is restricted by crystal orientation. By utilizing a spin-pair mechanism, the sensor's response dynamically aligns with the external magnetic field, enabling nanotesla sensitivity and alignment-free magnetometry at room temperature.
main_problem: Conventional color-center quantum sensors suffer from signal loss in off-axis magnetic fields because their spin quantization axes are fixed to the host lattice, limiting real-world applicability.
main_result: The use of the neutrally charged nitrogen-vacancy center ($	ext{NV}^0$) enables an isotropic magnetometer whose spin pair dynamically aligns with the external field, achieving nanotesla sensitivity at room temperature.
method: The system uses Spin-to-Charge (SC)-ODMR spectroscopy to read out the spin state of the $	ext{NV}^0$-dark spin pair, which exhibits field-direction independence.
model_or_system: The platform utilizes the $	ext{NV}^0$ center in diamond, specifically exploiting a spin-pair mechanism with an optically inactive dark spin. This pair's quantization axis dynamically aligns with the external magnetic field, providing an isotropic sensing mechanism.
key_observables: Resonance frequency of the central $|+1/2angle \leftrightarrow |−1/2angle$ transition, signal contrast, and coherence time ($T_2$).
important_parameters: Room temperature operation, nanotesla sensitivity, microsecond coherence time ($T_2 \approx 3 \mu	ext{s}$), and alignment-free operation.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the $	ext{NV}^0$-dark spin pair's spin selection rules result in a quantization axis that is rotationally invariant with respect to the external field.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dynamic alignment of the $	ext{NV}^0$-dark spin pair, the dual-band SC-ODMR readout mechanism, and field mapping demonstrating isotropic response across various orientations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the limitation of fixed-axis sensors to proposing the $	ext{NV}^0$-dark spin pair mechanism. It details spectroscopic measurements (SC-ODMR), validates the isotropic nature through field mapping, and confirms long coherence times using quantum control techniques.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it demonstrates a robust, solid-state quantum sensor operating at ambient conditions with long coherence times, pushing the boundaries of practical quantum sensing.
